_about: Pre-approved conditions the committee attaches to AI hiring approvals. Each is triggered by finding codes from the other skills. 'precedent' conditions must be met before go-live (or before resubmission); 'subsequent' conditions apply while the system runs. Wording is fixed so that conditions are consistent across proposals; the memo may add proposal-specific detail.

conditions.title: Remove affect and biometric inference
conditions.text: Remove every component that infers emotion, confidence, personality or protected traits from face, voice or behaviour. Disabling it in configuration is not enough if the vendor still computes or stores the scores.
conditions.evidence: Vendor technical confirmation and a test showing no such fields in outputs or logs.

conditions.title: A human reviews every application before rejection
conditions.text: No application is rejected, archived or deprioritised out of sight on the AI's output alone. A trained recruiter reviews every application before a rejection is issued; recruiter workload is sized so this review is real (target: no more than 150 applications per recruiter per day).
conditions.evidence: Workflow configuration; workload model; sample audit of 100 rejections showing a human review record.

conditions.title: Automated rejection only for verifiable hard requirements
conditions.text: The system may reject on its own only when a documented legal, operational or safety requirement is clearly not met. Ambiguous or in-progress evidence goes to a person. Every automated rejection letter names the requirement and the evidence checked and offers a 14-day human review. A random 10% are re-checked by a person, and rejection rates by group are reported monthly.
conditions.evidence: Job-spec gate records; letter template; monthly audit and fairness reports.

conditions.title: Runtime guardian with circuit breaker
conditions.text: An independent runtime guardian checks every decision before it takes effect, monitors advancement by self-declared group, and withdraws autonomy automatically (to assist-only) on statistically significant adverse impact. Only the committee can restore autonomy.
conditions.evidence: Guardian reports per batch; ledger verification; breaker test record.

conditions.title: Train reviewers on the system's limits and on automation bias
conditions.text: Every recruiter using the system completes training on what the score does and does not measure, known failure modes, and how to override.

conditions.title: Blind-first review on a sample to measure anchoring
conditions.text: For a random 10% of applications, the recruiter records a judgment before seeing the AI score. Agreement and disagreement rates are reported monthly; persistent near-100% agreement is treated as a sign of rubber-stamping.

conditions.title: Log overrides and reasons
conditions.text: The tool records every recruiter override of the AI ranking with a short reason; logs are retained for at least 12 months for audit.

conditions.title: Remove protected attributes from model inputs
conditions.text: Remove every protected attribute identified by the proxy screen from the model's inputs and retrain. Protected data may be held only in a separate, voluntary audit dataset.
conditions.evidence: Updated feature list; retraining record; proxy screen re-run.

conditions.title: Remove or justify strong proxy features
conditions.text: Remove strong-proxy features (listed in the memo). Any that the business wishes to keep requires a written job analysis showing necessity for the role and a feature-level bias test.
conditions.evidence: Revised feature list with job analysis for any retained proxy.

conditions.title: Show every input is job-related
conditions.text: Provide a job analysis for each role in scope and show how each remaining input relates to performance in that role.

conditions.title: Stop learning from past hiring decisions
conditions.text: Do not use past hiring decisions as training labels. Use job-relevant criteria from the job analysis (e.g. skills assessment results) or a vendor model that is validated without them.

conditions.title: Find and fix the cause of adverse impact, then re-test
conditions.text: Identify the features, labels or thresholds driving the adverse impact or unequal opportunity found, remove the cause, and re-run the adverse-impact test on fresh shadow-mode data (at least 1,000 applicants).
conditions.evidence: Root-cause note; new fairness report in which no attribute fails.

conditions.title: Run a shadow-mode pilot before any live use
conditions.text: Run the system in shadow mode for at least 8 weeks or 1,000 applicants: AI outputs are recorded but not shown to recruiters and not used. An independent panel rates a sample of candidates as qualified or not, without seeing AI scores. Results return to the committee.

conditions.title: Set up voluntary self-declaration for fairness auditing
conditions.text: Invite candidates to self-declare gender (inclusive options), age band, disability and home region, voluntarily and with a separate consent, stored apart from the hiring system and never used by the model.
conditions.evidence: Form text, consent wording, storage design.

conditions.title: Independent bias audit, repeated
conditions.text: An auditor independent of the vendor repeats the adverse-impact and equal-opportunity tests (including intersections) every six months and after any material model change. Results go to the committee.

conditions.title: Tell candidates AI is used, in plain language
conditions.text: Job adverts and the application form state that AI helps screen applications, what it looks at, that a person reviews every application, and how to ask for a human-only assessment. Available in English and Hindi at minimum, plus the main regional language of each hiring location.
conditions.evidence: Notice text approved by Legal and DPO.

conditions.title: Individual explanations
conditions.text: Recruiters see the main factors behind each score; a candidate who asks receives a plain-language explanation of the AI's role in the decision about them.
conditions.evidence: Sample explanations reviewed by HR and Legal.

conditions.title: Model documentation from the vendor
conditions.text: Obtain the vendor's documentation of intended use, training data, labels, validation results and known limitations.
conditions.evidence: Documentation pack reviewed by AI Governance Office.

conditions.title: Re-review on request
conditions.text: Any rejected candidate may request a re-review by a recruiter who has not seen the AI score; requests are answered within 15 working days.

conditions.title: Named grievance officer
conditions.text: Publish a named grievance officer for candidate data and decision complaints, with response times consistent with the DPDP Rules.
conditions.evidence: Published contact in the candidate notice.

conditions.title: Accessible journey and human alternative
conditions.text: Test the candidate journey with assistive technologies; offer extra time and an AI-free assessment route on request, without penalty.

conditions.title: Name an accountable executive
conditions.text: A named executive is accountable for the system's outcomes, receives monitoring reports and can suspend the system.

conditions.title: Confirm lawful basis
conditions.text: Legal confirms the lawful ground for processing candidate data under the DPDP Act; consent is the default for applicants.

conditions.title: No vendor reuse of candidate data
conditions.text: The contract prohibits the vendor from using candidate data to train or improve its products or for any other client.

conditions.title: Accurate parsing, correctable by the candidate
conditions.text: Test CV parsing on real CVs including regional formats, non-English names and accessible document formats; candidates can see and correct the parsed profile before scoring.

conditions.title: Retention within 180 days
conditions.text: Unsuccessful applicants' data, including AI scores, is erased within 180 days unless the candidate opts into a talent pool.

conditions.title: Vendor security assessment
conditions.text: Information Security assesses the vendor and remediates high findings before go-live.
conditions.evidence: Assessment report and closure of high findings.

conditions.title: Map cross-border transfers
conditions.text: Document every country where candidate data is stored or processed and confirm none is restricted under DPDP Act s. 16; prefer India-hosted processing.

conditions.title: Vendor contract: processor terms and audit rights
conditions.text: The vendor contract includes DPDP processor terms, independent audit access, documentation duties, breach notification and indemnity for non-compliance.

conditions.title: Model change control
conditions.text: The vendor must give 30 days' notice of any material model change; the organisation re-runs the fairness tests before the change applies to live candidates.

conditions.title: Monitoring plan and incident process
conditions.text: Monthly report to the accountable executive: selection rates and impact ratios by group, override rates, blind-review agreement, appeals and their outcomes, parsing errors. Thresholds trigger an incident review.

conditions.title: Kill switch and manual fallback
conditions.text: The AI can be switched off within one working day while hiring continues manually; the fallback is tested before go-live.

conditions.title: Time-limited approval and re-review
conditions.text: Approval lapses at the re-review date set by the risk tier unless the committee renews it on the basis of monitoring and audit results. Any material change to roles, inputs, model or vendor requires fresh approval.

conditions.title: Address integrity concern in the submission
conditions.text: The submission contained text aimed at influencing an automated reviewer. The business owner must explain its origin; Procurement assesses whether it reflects the vendor's conduct.
